pairs.difference: Both cards use the same quiet concentric-ring field (category 1), so the backdrop does not separate them. A's rings carry a dark corner falloff, 0.0137, inside the real range. B's yellow rings are clean at 0.0084. The difference is whimsy: B's bat has an invented cute face with shiny eyes, fangs and an open mouth, plus nub feet. No real card gives its object a character face. A's envelope has no invented face or mascot element.
pairs.fix: Draw the bat as a plain animal object with a simple dark head and small eyes. No smile, no open mouth, no cartoon character expression.

pairs.difference: A's cauldron stands on a chunky grey rock slab with cracks, chipped front facets and grain across the bottom third, at 0.0172, above the real 0.008 to 0.013. This reads as category 3 on a card whose peers use a plain ledge. B's shoes stand on a flat cream ledge against a flat orange wall, 0.0089, with only a cast shadow.
pairs.fix: Stand the cauldron on a smooth plain ledge in one soft colour, with one clean front edge and no cracks or rock texture.

pairs.difference: The numbers tie, but B's environment has more separate things: rail fence across both sides, rolling hills, distant tree clumps, pink clouds, a sunset sky and scattered grass tufts, plus curling vines and extra leaves spilling off the pumpkins. A's topiary has only a hedge band, one curved path, a lawn and a clear sky, which are a few large quiet shapes like the real birdhouse and coaster cards.
pairs.fix: Set the pumpkins on a plain lawn under a clear sky with one low distant hill line. Remove the fence, clouds, tree clumps, curling vines and most of the grass tufts.

pairs.difference: B's suitcase matches the suitcase in the real anchor sheet: sunburst wall, green boards, no props. A's column adds a large gold plaque on a post that covers the column's lower right, an orange plinth, wall moulding and a tiled floor strip. The crack across the shaft is invented story. At 0.0106 the background itself is quiet, so the case rests on the prop rather than on busyness.
pairs.fix: Remove the gold plaque and its post. Show the column alone on a simple plinth against a plain wall, with no crack.

pairs.difference: A's backdrop is quiet (0.0116, edges 0.013), but the ground around the stone piles on invented story: moss patches, cracks, a dirt mound, pebbles and leaf tufts at the base. B's slide has the busier background, with tile grid, pool edge and water rings, and its edges at 0.065 exceed the real 0.046. Those shapes all belong to a pool, though, not added decoration. The measurement points the other way, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Set the gravestone in plain smooth grass with no dirt mound, pebbles or leaf tufts, and remove the moss and cracks.

pairs.difference: B's teal wall repeats small broom silhouettes, so the backdrop motif copies the hero. It is tone-on-tone and measures quiet, but real backdrops use abstract rays, stripes, waves and diamonds, not icons of the object. A's mower sits on abstract concentric rings over a grass strip. Its daisies and tufts are small and low-key.
pairs.fix: Replace the broom wallpaper with soft plain diagonal stripes or a smooth wave pattern in two close teals, with no little brooms.

pairs.difference: A surrounds the house with story props: a large full moon, two twisted bare trees framing both edges, boulders and a hill. They form a staged scene rather than a quiet setting. B's door is the busier card, with dense small ivy across the top and both sides, and its edges at 0.107 exceed the real 0.089. Ivy density is B's real flaw, but it is one continuous mass in a simple setting. The numbers oppose this pick.
pairs.fix: Remove the moon, twisted trees and boulders. Keep the house on one smooth green hill under a plain blue sky with a few soft clouds.

pairs.difference: Both are category 1 hero objects floating on sunbursts with no props. A's purple rays are very clean, at 0.006 and edges 0.003, below the real minimums of 0.008 and 0.004, so the field looks emptier than real sunbursts. B's finer green rays with a dark vignette sit inside the range at 0.0115. The carved face belongs to a jack-o'-lantern and is not a finding. The evidence is thin.
pairs.fix: Give the sunburst a slightly stronger tone shift from centre to corners, with soft darker corners behind the pumpkin.

pairs.difference: A's crystal ball stands on a thick dark wooden shelf with visible grain, a lit top edge and a black underside band, plus an orange gradient wall. Its edges at 0.023 exceed the real 0.021. The ledge is a real material and a heavy dark band across the card. B's vending machine stands on a seamless purple sweep with almost nothing in the background, 0.0079, which is plain-ledge staging.
pairs.fix: Stand the ball on a smooth plain ledge in a lighter tone of the orange background, with no wood grain and no dark band.

pairs.difference: A's floor is large mottled flagstones with blotchy cracks and dark joints, 0.021 at the top of the real range, under a hard high-contrast green stripe wall. Floor and wall both compete with the coffin. B's plain plank floor and soft tone-on-tone blue stripes match the real suitcase card's staging, and its 0.0155 background is calmer.
pairs.fix: Lay the coffin on simple smooth floorboards in one warm tone, with soft low-contrast wall stripes and no mottled stone or cracks.

pairs.difference: A's candelabra sits on a tone-on-tone diamond field and B's lamp on a soft teal sunburst. Both patterns appear on real cards, both cards have no props and no invented decoration, and both measure inside the real range. Staging gives no reason to choose.

A's balloons float in plain blue sky with soft clouds along the bottom and right, very quiet at 0.0079. B's ship mixes a purple sunburst with a sea of white wave crests, and its edges at 0.049 are far above the listed 0.017. That range is a poor fit, because neither card is a pure graphic field. A real card also pairs rays with a real floor (the suitcase), and the waves belong to the ship's setting. There are no invented props on either card, so the call stays open.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away by over-staging, not by raw background busyness. They invent story around the hero: fences and clouds, moons and twisted trees, moss, pebbles and dirt mounds, plaques. They also harden the ground into textured material where real cards use plain ledges or simple planks, as with the cracked rock slab, grained dark shelf and mottled flagstones. Other tells are a cute character face (the bat) and a backdrop that repeats the hero as an icon (the broom wallpaper). Real cards stick to abstract tone-on-tone patterns and a few large quiet shapes. Caveat: the background measures do not separate reliably here. p05 and p07 run against my picks, and the non-generated-looking cards in p05, p07 and p12 exceed the real edge ranges. My low-confidence picks on p05, p07 and p08 lean partly on the Halloween subject matter, which is not staging evidence.
